alignments.note: Substantival adjective with a supplied generic noun and indefinite article; rule 24 prefers the substantive over the generic English noun.
No article morpheme is present, so the supplied *the* joins the noun (rule 15).
Italic *and*: no conjunction morpheme stands between the two verbs, so no morpheme licenses the coordinator (rule 14's closing sentences).
Niphal; the reflexive *himself* realizes the verb's own voice and stays with it (rule 44).
Italic *But*: the second line is juxtaposed with no conjunction in it, so the connective is supplied (rule 14).
Anarthrous substantival adjective takes the supplied *the* (rule 46), headed on the lexeme word.
*pass on* is the verb with its phrasal particle; the head stays on the verb (rule 44).
Third italic *and*: again no conjunction morpheme stands in the clause.
*suffer for it* is the ASV's whole rendering of the Niphal 'are punished'; dropping *for it* leaves *suffer*, which does not write the lexeme.

review_notes: Competing reading for t017-t018: marking *for it* added under rule 44's supplied-object clause; taken the other way because the bare *suffer* does not carry נֶעֱנָשׁוּ's sense and the phrase is one rendering rather than a supplied object beside a complete one.
All three of the ASV's connectives here are italic and answer to no waw; the count of conjunctions against connectives (rule 42's method) leaves the English side in surplus three times.
